AAA.description: Establish or restate the harmonic system from the specimen environment.

AAC.description: Increase harmonic tension without changing the harmonic jurisdiction itself.

AAG.description: Rotate voicing or upper-structure organization while preserving harmonic identity.

AAT.description: Temporarily remove explicit harmony; other jurisdictions continue without inheriting its exact job.

ACA.description: Establish or restate melodic contour logic.

ACC.description: Break melodic material into smaller cells while preserving ancestry.

ACG.description: Stretch melodic gestures across a larger time span.

ACT.description: Distribute melodic material across performers or timbres as a relay.

AGA.description: Establish the tuning or intonation rule.

AGC.description: Apply controlled pitch drift or microtonal displacement.

AGG.description: Flip the current consonance logic into its structured opposite.

AGT.description: Separate musical roles into strongly distinct registers.

ATA.description: Declare the pitch-bearing anchor or invariant as protected reference material.

ATC.description: Allow only the pitch aspect of the anchor to mutate while identity stays recognizable.

ATG.description: Required first codon. Initialize a specimen and reset local modifiers.

ATT.description: Convert pitch articulation into rhythmic or percussive function without simply becoming drums.

CAA.description: Establish or restate the base pulse.

CAC.description: Increase internal subdivision while the base pulse can remain stable.

CAG.description: Introduce another valid pulse or grouping so multiple rhythmic truths coexist.

CCA.description: Introduce additive or asymmetrical meter as an explicit timing jurisdiction.

CCC.description: Repeat the immediately active behavior; repetition strengthens memory and recognizability.

CCG.description: Increase apparent or literal speed according to current timing context.

CCT.description: Reduce apparent or literal speed while preserving other systems.

CGA.description: Increase event-arrival rate independently of BPM.

CGC.description: Decrease event-arrival rate without necessarily reducing tempo.

CGG.description: Shift one repeating process against another to change alignment and interference.

CGT.description: Create explicit silence or near-silence as structural material.

CTA.description: Pass timing responsibility between parts so no single source owns the whole phrase.

CTC.description: Maintain two incompatible temporal scales at once.

CTG.description: Change arrangement because an event occurs, not because a conventional section timer says so.

CTT.description: Cut directly to a new state with minimal transitional glue.

GAA.description: Establish the timbre and instrument palette from the environment.

GAC.description: Introduce a foreign sonic material that changes the palette by contact.

GAG.description: Swap functional roles between instruments or sound sources.

GAT.description: Strip away support and expose one stem or jurisdiction clearly.

GCA.description: Pull sound into dry, close, local space; reduce shared wash.

GCC.description: Increase spatial spread or reverberant field while preserving source identities.

GCG.description: Move energy, register, or spectral emphasis across the sound field.

GCT.description: Make recording-medium damage or lo-fi behavior causally affect the sound.

GGA.description: Establish the performance attitude from the environment.

GGG.description: Increase participation, intensity, or number of active agents without merely raising volume.

GGT.description: Let precision degrade into structured collapse while preserving traceable cause.

GTA.description: Introduce a new performer or population with its own job.

GTC.description: Create explicit call-and-response between distinct performers or populations.

GTG.description: Allow one role to borrow another role's behavior while remaining distinguishable.

GTT.description: Trigger group participation: chant, clap, response, swarm, or another social musical action.

TAA.description: Stop the currently foregrounded process locally; do not necessarily end the specimen.

TAC.description: Freeze the current anchor or system while a different active system changes around it.

TAG.description: Close the local phase, preserve accumulated scars, and clear temporary one-shot modifiers.

TAT.description: Make one jurisdiction obey another jurisdiction's mechanics without becoming it.

TCA.description: Compress current material or transformation into a smaller duration or space.

TCC.description: Stretch current material or transformation across a larger duration or space.

TCG.description: Invert a current relation, dependency, direction, or ordering rule.

TCT.description: Split a coherent active structure into still-related fragments.

TGA.description: Required final codon. End the specimen and freeze the final ledger.

TGC.description: Return to the recognizable anchor or invariant after mutation.

TGG.description: Rebuild the current organism after collapse while preserving ancestry and scars.

TGT.description: Temporarily remove one whole jurisdiction; remaining systems may not simply inherit its exact job.

TTA.description: Mark the next executable codon as mutation-protected.

TTC.description: Duplicate the previous executable behavior as a deliberate genetic repeat.

TTG.description: Mark the following local cassette as high-probability mutation territory until the next section boundary.

TTT.description: Fossilize the preceding local behavior or cassette so breeding preferentially preserves it.
